title: Railway catering company fined Rs. 500,000 for overcharging bottled water
byline: The Anuradhapura Magistrate’s Court has imposed a fine of Rs. 500,000 on Jayabima Catering, the railway canteen service operator, for selling bottled drinking water above the maximum retail price (MRP) on a train operating between Kankesanthurai and Anuradhapura.

title: Jailor’s evidence sensitive; don’t report in media: Magistrate
byline: Negombo Magistrate Selani Perera ordered the media to refrain from covering any of the evidence given by the Head Jailor of the Negombo Prison who testified at the magisterial inquiry into the recent clashes, since it contained sensitive information that could seriously endanger national security if revealed in public.

title: Fifa scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
byline: Fifa president Gianni Infantino says he has scrapped the controversial plan to sell off stakes in the governing body’s major competitions, following widespread opposition.

title: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga strikes historic Commonwealth gold in Javelin
byline: Sri Lanka’s 23-year-old javelin thrower, Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, made history by winning the gold medal in the Men’s Javelin Throw at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, ending the nation’s 20-year wait for a Commonwealth gold medal.

title: MoU to formalise Public-Private Partnership on e-waste management
byline: The Environment Ministry has announced that the Central Environmental Authority (CEA) and Dialog Axiata PLC will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Monday, August 3, to formalise a partnership for a nationwide electronic waste (e-waste) management programme.

title: Hotel Developers records profit after 7 years
byline: Hotel Developers (Lanka) Ltd (HDL), the state-owned enterprise and owner of the iconic Hilton Colombo, announced a significant financial turnaround, recording a profit after tax of Rs.48.5 million for the financial year ended 2025, marking the company’s first return to profitability, since 2017.

title: Improved IIF debt transparency ratings could unlock lower borrowing costs for Sri Lanka in global capital markets
byline: As Sri Lanka targets a return to international capital markets, its recent ascent as one of the fastest-improving sovereign nations in investor relations could prove to be a crucial financial asset.

title: Higher tea volumes meet sluggish demand at Colombo auction
byline:
The auction offerings totalled 6.0 million kilogrammes (M/Kgs), up from the 5.3 M/Kgs on offer the previous week. 
The Large and Semi-Leafy Orthodox teas realised a price advantage once again vis-à-vis the Orthodox/Rotovane BOP/BOPFs, which continued to witness a sluggish market.

title: Rescue operation expands as several fishing vessels report distress off Negombo
byline: Search and rescue teams have intensified operations off the coast of Negombo after several fishing vessels were reported to be in distress, with one vessel capsizing and leaving one person dead and two others missing.

title: Heavy rains submerge machinery brought to repair Peradeniya’s Devil’s Bridge
byline: Machinery and equipment brought to carry out repair work on the historic Devil’s Bridge in Peradeniya were submerged following the sharp rise in the Mahaweli River caused by heavy rainfall experienced over the past two days.

title: Cucurella gets tattoo of Spain coach to honour World Cup promise
byline: Spain defender Marc Cucurella proved he was a man of ​his word when he made good ‌his promise of getting a tattoo of his national team coach Luis ​de la Fuente’s face.

title: How Sri Lanka missed the opportunity to become a 200 billion dollar economy
byline: For the first time in history, Sri Lankan economy surpassed the hundred billion dollar mark in 2025. Gross Domestic Product (“GDP”) and GDP per capita reached USD 109 billion and USD 5,003 respectively in 2025. Interestingly, Sri Lanka was an 85 billion economy way back in 2015, and it took a decade to surpass the hundred billion dollar benchmark. This suggests a decade of slow economic progress.

title: Metro bus service to expand to Jaffna, Kandy by year-end: Minister
byline: Transport Minister Bimal Ratnayake says the government’s Metro bus service will be expanded to Jaffna and Kandy before the end of this year, with a fresh fleet of buses set to enter service in the coming weeks.

title: US to make visa bond program permanent for people from dozens of countries
byline: The U.S. State Department will make permanent a visa bond program ‌that could require applicants from 50 countries, mostly from Africa, to post bonds of up to $20,000 when seeking U.S. visas, according to a federal notice, posted online on Friday.

title: 17 empty shipping containers fall overboard off Colombo
byline: Seventeen empty shipping containers fell into the sea from the Maldives-flagged cargo vessel MV MSS GRAPHENE within the outer harbour limits of Colombo early this morning, 1 August 2026.

title: Station Masters warn of safety risks over unresolved signal failures
byline: The Sri Lanka Railway Station Masters’ Association (SLRSMA) has raised serious concerns over unresolved signaling failures across several railway sections, warning that continued train operations under temporary arrangements could jeopardize passenger safety.

title: Tuition classes, seminars banned ahead of grade 5, A/L exams
byline: The Examinations Department has imposed a ban on tuition classes, seminars and other examination-related activities ahead of the 2026 Grade 5 Scholarship and G.C.E. Advanced Level (A/L) examinations.

title: Ravi, Shani could face stronger charges over Easter Sunday attacks, says Gammanpila
byline: In the wake of former IGP Pujith Jayasundara and former Defence Secretary Hemasiri Fernando being sentenced to death for failing to prevent the Easter Sunday bomb attacks, Pivithuru Hela Urumaya (PHU) leader Udaya Gammanpila claimed that similar or even stronger charges could be brought against Public Security Ministry Secretary Ravi Seneviratne and CID Director Shani Abeysekara.

title: Update: Inmate dies following unrest at Mahara Prison
byline: An unrest was reported inside Mahara Prison, prompting authorities to deploy additional security forces to the area.

title: President AKD congratulates Rumesh on Commonwealth Games gold
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has congratulated Sri Lankan athlete Rumesh Tharanga on winning the men’s javelin gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, describing the achievement as the fulfilment of the nation’s “golden dream.”

title: CPID holds inaugural youth empowerment workshop
byline: The Centre for Policy Innovation and Development (CPID) successfully concluded its inaugural workshop titled ’’Empowering the Youth in a Changing World: Opportunities from China–Sri Lanka Cooperation,’’ bringing together 45 emerging young leaders from diverse professional, academic, and social backgrounds.

title: NPP decision-making process unclear, says Lal Wijenayake
byline: Senior lawyer Lal Wijenayake has questioned the National People’s Power’s (NPP) internal decision-making process, saying he is accustomed to the consultative tradition of leftist politics but is uncertain how decisions are taken within the ruling coalition.

title: Cannabis worth Rs. 106m seized in air cargo
byline: Sri Lanka Customs has detected more than 10.6 kilograms of suspected cannabis-based narcotics concealed inside an air cargo consignment that arrived from Bangkok, Thailand.

title: Man injured in Rathmalana shooting
byline: A man was injured in a shooting incident reported on Kandawala Road in Rathmalana this afternoon.

title: Minor flood warning issued for low-lying areas of Kelani River valley
byline: The Irrigation Department has issued a warning for minor flood situation within the next 48 hours in the low-lying areas of the Kelani River valley.

title: US to make visa bond program permanent for people from dozens of countries
byline: The U.S. State Department will make permanent a visa bond program ‌that could require applicants from 50 countries, mostly from Africa, to post bonds of up to $20,000 when seeking U.S. visas, according to a federal notice, posted online on Friday.

title: Curfew imposed in Ragama Police Division
byline: Sri Lanka Police have imposed a curfew within the Ragama Police Division. Police said that the restriction will remain in effect until further notice.

title: India team to arrive in Sri Lanka on August 4 for Test series
byline: The Indian cricket team is scheduled to arrive in Sri Lanka on August 4 ahead of their upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka.

title: Fresh unrest erupts outside Mahara Prison
byline: Fresh unrest has been reported in the vicinity of Mahara Prison. Tensions escalated after several sounds resembling gunfire were heard from inside the prison, prompting relatives who had arrived to visit inmates and nearby residents to attempt to break through police barricades.
